mbm-1026.clue: My goldfish swims when the kettle boils.
mbm-1026.quote: I cut a bright paper fish for the kitchen window. Steam from the kettle lifts its tail away from the glass. On cold mornings it seems to swim right through the garden.

mbm-1027.clue: One of my socks is quite famous.
mbm-1027.quote: I crocheted a giant striped sock to hold our spare yarn. At craft night the whole basket disappeared inside. Now people ask how the sock is doing before they ask after me.

mbm-1028.clue: I like tossing a disc after dark.
mbm-1028.quote: A glow-in-the-dark disc draws a green loop across our evening game. Between throws I can hear my friends, but all I can see is the disc traveling from one laugh to another.

mbm-1029.quote: One painting shows our blue kitchen chair in morning light. In the other the chair is empty at dusk, except for my father’s cap. Mum hangs them on opposite sides of the same doorway.

mbm-1030.clue: I borrowed the sunset for my scarf trick.
mbm-1030.quote: At the picnic I juggled three silk scarves in orange, pink and violet. Against the real sunset the violet one nearly disappeared. I caught it because a friend pointed where to look.

mbm-1031.quote: I was painting wild plums and dipped my wet blue brush in the pink. The resulting purple looked exactly like the stain the fruit left on my fingertips. I kept the mistake on my palette.

mbm-1032.clue: I swim the slow length last.
mbm-1032.quote: At the far end of the outdoor pool a vine hangs over the wall. I float on my back under the leaves after my laps. It’s the only ceiling I’ve ever missed in winter.

mbm-1033.clue: The old accordion has a secret admirer.
mbm-1033.quote: At our vallenato rehearsal the upstairs neighbor lowers a basket of limes whenever we play her favorite tune. We tie one lime ribbon to the accordion strap before the next verse.

mbm-1034.clue: I keep my juggling clubs in pillowcases.
mbm-1034.quote: I stitched different fabric cases to stop the paint chipping in transit. A kid asked me to juggle the cases instead. Three empty pillowcases make an impressively floppy finale.

mbm-1035.clue: I found the blue on the underside.
mbm-1035.quote: I painted an old fishing boat from the pier until the light changed. When its owner hauled it out I discovered the prettiest blue underneath. He held it there until I’d mixed the color.

mbm-1036.quote: I take a folded white parasol to the sunny terrace. My sister painted a gray cloud underneath it. When I wake up beneath the thing I always check whether I’ve slept through the weather.

mbm-1037.clue: I collect chalk handprints on brown paper.
mbm-1037.quote: After my first clean lift I pressed my chalky palm onto a grocery bag. My training partner put his beside it. It looks like two ghosts high-fiving in a gym that’s closed for the night.

mbm-1038.quote: I kept finding lion-shaped door knockers while sightseeing and started drawing a map of them. My favorite was a tiny sleeping lion on a florist’s back door, with pollen stuck to his nose.

mbm-1039.clue: I bring a round mirror on walking tours.
mbm-1039.quote: I watched the painted ceiling of an old arcade in that mirror while walking through. A swan and a whole cloud of cherubs followed me across the tiles without giving me a stiff neck.

mbm-1040.clue: I drew the engine in raindrops.
mbm-1040.quote: The train window fogged so thickly I could only see through a patch I wiped with my sleeve. I traced a little locomotive in the mist. The real train passed through its wheels.

mbm-1041.clue: I mailed myself the shortest street.
mbm-1041.quote: I bought a postcard on a lane barely wider than my arms. I posted it from the box at the far end, then raced it home. I won, but the postcard got the better stamp.

mbm-1042.clue: I know the bath by its moss.
mbm-1042.quote: At the outdoor onsen a bright cushion of moss holds a single red maple leaf. I rest my chin by the water and watch the leaf quiver whenever the wooden spout refills.

mbm-1043.clue: Our anime club repairs things very slowly.
mbm-1043.quote: We paused a movie to draw a mechanic’s toolkit. Everybody invented one tool the original artist had left out. My contribution was a tiny wrench shaped to fit a robot’s stubborn eyebrow.

mbm-1044.clue: I painted with a frozen brush once.
mbm-1044.quote: I went out to paint the winter orchard before the sun woke. My brush froze into a stiff little rake that made perfect bare branches. I kept painting until I could feel my fingers again.

mbm-1045.clue: I know when the crowd will gasp.
mbm-1045.quote: I’ve seen the village cinema’s adventure serial five times. At the cliff scene I watch the front row instead of the screen. Last Friday three people grabbed the exact same armrest.

mbm-1046.clue: I play one extra point for the footprints.
mbm-1046.quote: After the last rally the sand is full of stops and starts. My partner and I try to trace our longest exchange backward from the net before the tide rubs it away.

mbm-1047.clue: I’ve got a contact card with a coffee bean on it.
mbm-1047.quote: I talked to a radio operator who roasts coffee before sunrise. Her confirmation card arrived smelling faintly of the cupboard where she’d kept it. I tuned in next week with a cup ready.

mbm-1048.clue: My sister says I bought the wrong ending twice.
mbm-1048.quote: I bought two old copies of the same mystery. One cover has a skull, the other a pair of bananas. My sister and I read them side by side. She thought the inspector was funny a whole chapter before I did.

mbm-1049.clue: I reuse the best tent peg.
mbm-1049.quote: My dad carved one of our pegs from a fallen branch and left a little face on its head. At each campground I take a portrait of that face with a different sunrise behind it.

mbm-1050.clue: I hid a stanza in my jacket.
mbm-1050.quote: I liked a poem so much I copied it on a square of cloth and stitched it inside my pocket. When the bus is late I turn the pocket inside out and read at the stop.
